# Resource: stripe_issuing_card

A virtual card issued to a cardholder. Stripe issues cards only for a platform's connected accounts, so manage cards through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is a connected account with the `card_issuing` capability active, and set `financial_account` to a Treasury financial account of that account with its `card_issuing` feature active. A new card is `inactive`. Set `status` to `active` once the cardholder's review has finished, and back to `inactive` to pause it. `number` and `cvc` hold the full card number and CVC, which Stripe returns on request for a virtual card; they are sensitive.

~> Stripe cannot delete a card, so `terraform destroy` cancels it, and the canceled card stays on the connected account. Canceling is final: a card whose `status` is `canceled` cannot be activated again, and Stripe refuses the change. Changing `cardholder`, `currency`, `type`, `financial_account` or any other field Stripe takes only on create replaces the card, which cancels the old one and issues a new number.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "issuing_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "A connected account with the card_issuing and treasury capabilities active."
}

variable "cardholder" {
  type        = string
  description = "The cardholder the card is issued to."
}

# Issuing runs on a connected account, so a second provider configuration acts on it.
provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "issuing"
  stripe_account = var.issuing_account
}

# Cards on a connected account draw on one of its Treasury financial accounts.
resource "stripe_treasury_financial_account" "cards" {
  provider             = stripe.issuing
  supported_currencies = ["usd"]
  features = {
    card_issuing = { requested = true }
  }
}

resource "stripe_issuing_card" "travel" {
  provider          = stripe.issuing
  cardholder        = var.cardholder
  currency          = "usd"
  type              = "virtual"
  financial_account = stripe_treasury_financial_account.cards.id

  # A new card is inactive. Set status = "active" once the cardholder's review has finished.

  spending_controls = {
    spending_limits = [{ amount = 20000, interval = "daily" }]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `cardholder` - (Required) The [Cardholder](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_cardholder_object) object with which the card will be associated. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `currency` - (Required) The currency for the card. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `type` - (Required) The type of card to issue. Possible values are `physical` or `virtual`. Possible values: `physical`, `virtual`. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `cancellation_reason` - (Optional) Reason why the `status` of this card is `canceled`. Possible values: `lost`, `stolen`.
* `exp_month` - (Optional) The desired expiration month (1-12) for this card if [specifying a custom expiration date](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/cards/virtual/issue-cards?testing-method=with-code#exp-dates). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `exp_year` - (Optional) The desired 4-digit expiration year for this card if [specifying a custom expiration date](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/cards/virtual/issue-cards?testing-method=with-code#exp-dates). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `financial_account` - (Optional) The new financial account ID the card will be associated with. This field allows a card to be reassigned to a different financial account. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `lifecycle_controls` - (Optional) Rules that control the lifecycle of this card, such as automatic cancellation. Refer to our [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/controls/lifecycle-controls) for more details. Changing it replaces the resource. See [`lifecycle_controls`](#lifecycle_controls) below.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `replacement_for` - (Optional) The card this is meant to be a replacement for (if any). Changing it replaces the resource.
* `replacement_reason` - (Optional) If `replacement_for` is specified, this should indicate why that card is being replaced. Possible values: `damaged`, `expired`, `lost`, `stolen`. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `spending_controls` - (Optional) Rules that control spending for this card. Refer to our [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/controls/spending-controls) for more details. See [`spending_controls`](#spending_controls) below.
* `status` - (Optional) Whether authorizations can be approved on this card. May be blocked from activating cards depending on past-due Cardholder requirements. Defaults to `inactive`. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`.

<a id="lifecycle_controls"></a>
### `lifecycle_controls`

The `lifecycle_controls` attribute supports:

* `cancel_after` - (Required) See [`lifecycle_controls.cancel_after`](#lifecycle_controls.cancel_after) below.

<a id="lifecycle_controls.cancel_after"></a>
### `lifecycle_controls.cancel_after`

The `lifecycle_controls.cancel_after` attribute supports:

* `payment_count` - (Required) The card is automatically cancelled when it makes this number of non-zero payment authorizations and transactions. The count includes penny authorizations, but doesn't include non-payment actions, such as authorization advice.

<a id="spending_controls"></a>
### `spending_controls`

The `spending_controls` attribute supports:

* `allowed_card_presences` - (Optional) Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be allowed. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. All other statuses will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `allowed_categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to allow. All other categories will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_categories`.
* `allowed_merchant_countries` - (Optional) Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be allowed. Authorizations from merchants in all other countries will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `blocked_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_card_presences` - (Optional) Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be declined. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. Cannot be set with `allowed_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to decline. All other categories will be allowed. Cannot be set with `allowed_categories`.
* `blocked_merchant_countries` - (Optional) Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `allowed_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `spending_limits` - (Optional) Limit spending with amount-based rules that apply across any cards this card replaced (i.e., its `replacement_for` card and _that_ card's `replacement_for` card, up the chain). See [`spending_controls.spending_limits`](#spending_controls.spending_limits) below.
* `spending_limits_currency` - (Read-Only) Currency of the amounts within `spending_limits`. Always the same as the currency of the card.

<a id="spending_controls.spending_limits"></a>
### `spending_controls.spending_limits`

The `spending_controls.spending_limits` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - (Required) Maximum amount allowed to spend per interval. This amount is in the card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `categories` - (Optional) Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) this limit applies to. Omitting this field will apply the limit to all categories.
* `interval` - (Required) Interval (or event) to which the amount applies. Possible values: `all_time`, `daily`, `monthly`, `per_authorization`, `weekly`, `yearly`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `brand` - The brand of the card.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `cvc` - (Sensitive) The card's CVC. For security reasons, this is only available for virtual cards, and will be omitted unless you explicitly request it with [the `expand` parameter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/expanding_objects). Additionally, it's only available via the ["Retrieve a card" endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/cards/retrieve), not via "List all cards" or any other endpoint.
* `last4` - The last 4 digits of the card number.
* `latest_fraud_warning` - Stripe’s assessment of whether this card’s details have been compromised. If this property isn't null, cancel and reissue the card to prevent fraudulent activity risk. See [`latest_fraud_warning`](#latest_fraud_warning) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `number` - (Sensitive) The full unredacted card number. For security reasons, this is only available for virtual cards, and will be omitted unless you explicitly request it with [the `expand` parameter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/expanding_objects). Additionally, it's only available via the ["Retrieve a card" endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/cards/retrieve), not via "List all cards" or any other endpoint.
* `replaced_by` - The latest card that replaces this card, if any.
* `wallets` - Information relating to digital wallets (like Apple Pay and Google Pay). See [`wallets`](#wallets) below.

<a id="latest_fraud_warning"></a>
### `latest_fraud_warning`

The `latest_fraud_warning` attribute supports:

* `started_at` - Timestamp of the most recent fraud warning.
* `type` - The type of fraud warning that most recently took place on this card. This field updates with every new fraud warning, so the value changes over time. If populated, cancel and reissue the card. Possible values: `card_testing_exposure`, `fraud_dispute_filed`, `third_party_reported`, `user_indicated_fraud`.

<a id="wallets"></a>
### `wallets`

The `wallets` attribute supports:

* `apple_pay` - See [`wallets.apple_pay`](#wallets.apple_pay) below.
* `google_pay` - See [`wallets.google_pay`](#wallets.google_pay) below.
* `primary_account_identifier` - Unique identifier for a card used with digital wallets

<a id="wallets.apple_pay"></a>
### `wallets.apple_pay`

The `wallets.apple_pay` attribute supports:

* `eligible` - Apple Pay Eligibility
* `ineligible_reason` - Reason the card is ineligible for Apple Pay Possible values: `missing_agreement`, `missing_cardholder_contact`, `unsupported_region`.

<a id="wallets.google_pay"></a>
### `wallets.google_pay`

The `wallets.google_pay` attribute supports:

* `eligible` - Google Pay Eligibility
* `ineligible_reason` - Reason the card is ineligible for Google Pay Possible values: `missing_agreement`, `missing_cardholder_contact`, `unsupported_region`.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

Run the import where the resource's `provider` acts on the connected account that holds it.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import an issuing card using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_issuing_card.travel
  id = "ic_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixn6uuO0Xu"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_issuing_card.travel
  identity = {
    id = "ic_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixn6uuO0Xu"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the issuing card.

Using `terraform import`, import an issuing card using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_issuing_card.travel ic_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixn6uuO0Xu
```
